confidence_notes: Restaurant anchors rest on aggregated 2026 estimates from combien-coute.net, which draws on Numbeo crowd data, plus national espresso data from a CRC/Assoutenti study. Those are secondary sources, not Rimini-specific surveys. The cappuccino figure is a blend of the Numbeo average (about EUR 2.02) and a travel-guide standing-to-seated range. Beer uses the Numbeo 0.5 L draft price (EUR 5) scaled to a standard serving. Cocktail and wine are weaker: no direct local price was found, so cocktail is set at about 2x the beer anchor and wine at about EUR 5 per glass, roughly 1.1x beer. Accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates for July peak season. No live booking pages or current listings were inspected, and no accommodation searches were run. EUR values were converted to USD at an assumed rate of about 1.15 USD per EUR from model knowledge, not from a retrieved source. The FX observation is the RBA USD per AUD figure of 0.7088 for 2026-03-20, reported in search results from the RBA exchange-rates page; I did not open that page and did not confirm a newer RBA observation, so it is roughly seven months older than the 2026-10-16 generation date. OFX market rates were not used.
comparable_city_reasoning: No comparable city was needed. Rimini was treated directly as an Adriatic beach resort in Emilia-Romagna. Restaurant and coffee anchors come from the 2026 Rimini estimates described above, with a national espresso benchmark as a cross-check. Cocktail and wine use the local price relationship to beer because direct data was weak.
